battle.name: 委內瑞拉獨立戰爭
battle.theater: 委內瑞拉中部卡拉布索戰場
battle.brief: 1811年4月19日卡拉卡斯首倡獨立，委內瑞拉獨立戰爭由此爆發，先後經三屆共和國、二度淪陷與玻利瓦爾的安第斯縱走，最終在1821年6月24日卡拉布索戰役定勝。卡面輪發槍屬十六世紀西班牙火繩式後膛手槍，1811年已被燧發手槍取代，只在軍官隨身自衛的傳統上延續。

kit.name: 輪發槍
kit.history: 最早的後膛手槍。機械太貴，只給火槍隊的軍官與衛兵。

countries: 這場戰爭是西班牙王國的美洲殖民地與其美洲屬地叛軍之間長達十四年的內戰，交戰方與指揮系統前後換過幾輪。叛軍一方在1811年以城市自治市為骨架組建聯邦式架構：加拉加斯、瓦倫西亞、庫馬納、巴里納斯、馬加里塔等市各自宣佈自治並組織民兵，1811年7月5日組成第一共和國，即委內瑞拉共和國，由弗朗西斯科·德·米蘭達以最高統帥身分主持，玻利瓦爾以准將身分列名其下，軍政實權分散在各市的最高政府與地方民兵指揮部，因此第一共和國是一個以城市民兵為骨架、帶聯邦色彩的臨時政權。1813年米蘭達在波多黎各海域被俘之後，第二共和國在委內瑞拉東部成立，仍由玻利瓦爾任最高統帥；1814年再成第三共和國；1819年玻利瓦爾在新格拉那達作戰，12月組成大哥倫比亞聯邦，中樞一度設於奧里諾科河畔的安戈斯圖拉。王黨一方是委內瑞拉都督區與卡斯塔利亞系軍區的常備軍，骨幹是固定團，另有王室志願兵營與殖民地白人民兵組成的獵兵營，騎兵主力為長矛騎兵團；1811年從西班牙本土運來的援軍由巴勃羅·德·拉·莫拉萊哈率領，1814年後由米格爾·德·拉·托雷接掌，新格拉那達方向則由何塞·瑪麗亞·巴雷羅與總督安東尼奧·卡瓦耶羅-貢戈拉主持。第三方力量亦有牽動：海地佩蒂安政府以火槍、款項與印刷所支援流亡的玻利瓦爾，荷屬庫拉索與英屬安的列斯商人向叛軍出售火槍、火藥與硝石，而西班牙本土的波旁王朝在拿破崙戰爭中被牽制，無力有效增援美洲。
countriesEn: This war was a fourteen-year civil war between the Spanish monarchy's American colony and the rebels of its own American territories, and both the belligerents and the command structures changed several times over. On the rebel side, a federal framework was built in 1811 on the skeleton of the city municipalities: Caracas, Valencia, Cumaná, Barinas and Margarita each declared its own autonomy and organised its militia, and on 5 July 1811 they formed the First Republic, the Republic of Venezuela, presided over by Francisco de Miranda as Generalísimo, with Bolívar listed below him as a brigadier, while actual military and political authority remained dispersed among the municipal supremos and the local militia commands; the First Republic was therefore a provisional government built on urban militia and coloured by federalism. After Miranda was captured in the waters of Puerto Rico in 1813, the Second Republic was proclaimed in eastern Venezuela, again with Bolívar as supreme chief; 1814 brought the Third Republic; and in 1819, while campaigning in New Granada, Bolívar formed the Gran Colombia federation in December, its seat for a time at Angostura on the Orinoco. On the royalist side stood the permanent army of the Audiencia of Caracas and the Captaincy General of Venezuela, its backbone the Regimiento Fijo, with the Batallón de Voluntarios Realistas and the white colonial militia brigades of cazadores, and the lancers as the main cavalry arm: the reinforcements shipped from metropolitan Spain in 1811 were led by Pablo de la Moraleja, and from 1814 the command passed to Miguel de la Torre, while in the New Granada direction the field was held by José María Barreiro under the viceroy Antonio Caballero y Góngora. Third parties were drawn in as well: the government of Pétion in Haiti supplied the exiled Bolívar with muskets, money and a printing press, merchants in Dutch Curaçao and the British Antilles sold muskets, powder and saltpetre to the insurgents, and the Bourbon monarchy in Spain, absorbed by the Napoleonic war, was in no position to reinforce its American possessions effectively.
people: 關鍵人物可分四類。第一類是王黨將領：莫拉萊哈率援軍於1811年抵達委內瑞拉，主持對叛軍的第一輪攻勢；米格爾·德·拉·托雷在1814至1816年間接掌王黨軍，擊垮第三共和國；何塞·托馬斯·博韋斯是西班牙北部阿斯圖里亞斯人，早年在西班牙軍的騎兵隊服役，1814年率長矛騎兵隊越過安第斯山，以安第斯暴君之名在山區主導殲滅戰，1815年4月在王之野地一役失利後不久死於傷勢；1819年波哥大方向由巴雷羅率軍把守，並於8月7日的波亞卡被玻利瓦爾擊潰。第二類是叛軍領袖：米蘭達出生於加拉加斯，參加過美國獨立戰爭與法國大革命，1810年回國後在卡拉加斯公報上公開主張共和與武裝，是第一共和國的靈魂人物，1813年7月在波多黎各海岸被西班牙海軍俘虜，囚於加的斯的拉卡拉卡要塞，次年死在獄中；玻利瓦爾1783年生於加拉加斯，1810年在波多黎各戰役初戰，1811年7月被任命為共和軍准將，1813年被米蘭達稱為解放者，此後率軍東進、越安第斯、戰波哥大、打卡拉布索，最後打到秘魯的胡寧與阿亞庫喬。第三類是地方首領與技術骨幹：巴里納斯人何塞·安東尼奧·帕埃斯原為西班牙軍官，1819年末帶著平原騎兵加入玻利瓦爾，1821年6月28日在拉斯克薩雷拉斯的中央以長矛密集衝鋒擊穿王黨翼側；安東尼奧·何塞·蘇克雷在卡拉布索以中央高地的佯攻牽制王黨右翼；托馬斯·玻利瓦爾則把門重砲推上陡坡，旁觀者一度懷疑這究竟是勇敢還是愚蠢。第四類是援助者與象徵人物：海地總統佩蒂安提供了槍械、款項與印刷所；1811年4月19日刊出獨立宣言的是胡安·赫爾曼·羅西奧，第一共和國成立時留下的法律文件則出自他的手筆。
peopleEn: The key figures fall into four groups. The first are the royalist commanders: Moraleja arrived in Venezuela with the reinforcements in 1811 and directed the first counter-offensive against the insurgents; Miguel de la Torre took command of the royalist army between 1814 and 1816 and crushed the Third Republic; José Tomás Boves was an Asturian from northern Spain who had served in a cavalry regiment of the Spanish army, and in 1814 he led his lancers across the Andes, and under the name of the Tyrant of the Andes directed a war of annihilation in the mountain zone, dying of his wounds shortly after his defeat at the Campo del Rey in April 1815; the New Granada side was held in 1819 by Barreiro, who was beaten by Bolívar at Boyacá on 7 August. The second group are the rebel leaders: Miranda was born in Caracas, served in the American War of Independence and in the French Revolution, and after returning home in 1810 argued openly for a republic and for armed citizens in the Gaceta de Caracas; he was the soul of the First Republic, was taken by a Spanish squadron off the coast of Puerto Rico in July 1813, and died the following year in the fortress of La Carraca at Cádiz, where he was imprisoned. Bolívar was born in Caracas in 1783, saw his first action in the Puerto Rico campaign of 1810, was made a brigadier of the republican army in July 1811, was named the Liberator by Miranda in 1813, and then led his armies east, over the Andes, against Bogotá, at Carabobo, and finally into Peru at Junín and Ayacucho. The third group are the local caudillos and the technical spine of the army: José Antonio Páez, a man of Barinas who had been an officer in the Spanish service, brought his llanero horse into Bolívar's ranks at the end of 1819 and on 28 June 1821 broke the royalist flank with a massed lance charge at Las Queseras del Medio; Antonio José de Sucre pinned the royalist right with a feint on the central heights at Carabobo; and Tomás Bolívar pushed a heavy gun up a steep slope, at which the onlookers wondered whether this was courage or folly. The fourth group are the patrons and the symbolic figures: President Pétion of Haiti supplied the muskets, the money and the printing press, and the manifesto of 19 April 1811 was published by Juan Germán Roscio, who also drew up the legal acts by which the First Republic came into being.
kits: 卡面這件輪發槍是十六世紀初的西班牙後膛手槍：以彈簧驅動的燧石輪打擊狗口夾持的慢火繩點燃火藥，機件昂貴，只配給火槍隊的軍官與近衛。因此到了1811年，它早已被燧發手槍取代，戰場上不可能再出現輪發槍，它代表的是西班牙軍官身佩副武器這條延續了三百年的傳統，而1811年真正在軍官腰上的是燧發手槍，火炮組另配短管手槍與通條。真正左右戰局的火器是前膛燧發滑膛步槍：西班牙線列步兵用一點五八英寸口徑的褐色貝松型與零點四一七英寸的瓦倫西型，叛軍與平原騎兵多英式滑膛步槍，如零點五七七英寸的褐色貝斯型，另有燧發卡賓槍；雙方都配刺刀，褐色貝斯型配插式刺刀，零點四一七型配套筒刺刀，刺刀在密集縱隊的白刃戰裡仍是最要命的一環。騎兵是這場戰爭最吃重的兵種：王黨長矛騎兵用長矛與半長矛，制式矛是1799年西班牙軍列裝的帕拉福克斯型；叛軍的平原騎兵則以馬刀、卡賓槍與砍刀並行，近身靠馬刀砍殺，遠射靠火槍。砲兵方面，交戰雙方都裝備四磅、六磅、八磅野砲與十二磅攻城砲，砲車以前車牽引，配備用砲與彈藥車；彈藥裝在紙包內，步兵腰繫皮帶與盒子，火藥由王黨軍在波多黎各與加的斯的火藥廠供給，叛軍則主要靠庫拉索與英屬安的列斯的商船取得火藥、硝石與鉛彈。運輸上，叛軍靠奧里諾科河與支流的船隻把軍火從海運到內陸，平原馬匹是主要的機動與載重工具；王黨靠加勒比海沿岸的港口與近海帆船維持補給，越過安第斯山區的補給線最為脆弱。
kitsEn: The wheellock pistol on the card is an early sixteenth-century Spanish breech-loading pistol: a spring-driven pyrite wheel strikes against the slow match held in the jaws of the dog, setting the powder alight, and the mechanism is so costly that it was issued only to officers of the musketeers and to the guards. By 1811 it had long been superseded by the flintlock pistol and could no longer appear on any battlefield; what it represents is the three-hundred-year-old tradition of the Spanish officer carrying a sidearm, and the pistol actually at an officer's belt in 1811 was a flintlock, with artillery crews issued short-barrelled pistols and their linstocks. The weapons that actually decided the war were flintlock smoothbore muskets: the Spanish line infantry used the 1.58-inch Brown Besson pattern and the 0.417-inch Valenciennes pattern, while the insurgents and the llanero horse carried English-pattern smoothbores such as the 0.577-inch Brown Bess, together with flintlock carbines; both sides bore bayonets, socket bayonets for the Brown Bess and plug bayonets for the 0.417 pattern, and the bayonet remained the most lethal arm in the close fighting of packed columns. Cavalry was the most heavily weighted arm of this war: the royalist lancers used full lances and half-lances, the service lance being the Palafox pattern adopted by the Spanish army in 1799, while the rebel llaneros worked with sabres, carbines and machetes together, cutting at close quarters with the sabre and shooting at range with the musket. On the artillery side both parties fielded 4-, 6-, 8-pounder field guns and 12-pounder siege pieces, the guns being drawn by limbers and accompanied by spare guns and caissons; ammunition was carried in paper cartridges, with cartridge boxes and waist belts slung on the infantry, powder supplied to the royalists by the magazines of Puerto Rico and Cádiz, and the insurgents dependent on Dutch and British merchantmen for powder, saltpetre and round lead. In transport terms the insurgents ran their ammunition inland on boats and lighters along the Orinoco and its tributaries, and llanero horses were their chief means of movement and of carrying loads; the royalists fed their army from the ports of the Caribbean and their coastal craft, and their line of supply across the Andean crossings was by far the most fragile of the two.
tactics: 整場戰爭有三套戰術體系。1811年的起義是城市民兵式：加拉加斯的民兵在街壘後列陣，以火槍齊射與刺刀反衝對付王黨縱隊；米蘭達在1811年6月以約一千出頭的兵力攻打卡貝略港，守軍不足五百、依城牆與砲位固守，攻方屢次受挫而退，這次失敗使第一共和國失去北進的支點。1812年王黨改為旱季攻勢：委內瑞拉一年分旱、雨兩季，王黨的作戰季節在12月至翌年5月，靠平原騎兵在夏季沼澤與河汊間的行動力避開雨季；1812年3月26日卡拉斯遭遇極強地震，城垣、兵營與軍械庫多毀，王黨軍在震後迅速南下，於4月再奪瓦倫西亞，叛軍節節退向海岸，米蘭達最終在1812年7月離境，1814年王黨得以恢復對北部海岸線的全面控制，這靠的不是攻城技術，而是旱季的時間窗口。1813至1815年，玻利瓦爾在東部重建軍隊，於1813年4月發布至死方休令，其部隊在奪回首都後處決了數百名被俘的王黨軍官，數字各家不一；王黨的反擊由博韋斯的長矛騎兵主導，長矛衝鋒在山區窄路上能瓦解密集步兵縱隊，1814年6月拉普艾塔與9月埃爾托波兩役之後，第三共和國的軍隊被消耗殆盡。真正反轉的是1816年後的持久戰：玻利瓦爾退入奧里諾科流域，用一間茅屋、一張木匠做的桌子、一座印刷所維持軍政府的運作，頒布土地與解放黑奴的法令，靠一條河的船運維持補給；1819年他率約兩千人自安戈斯圖拉溯河而上再翻越安第斯，8月7日在波亞卡擊潰巴雷羅，10月進入波哥大；1820年轉戰北方戰線，同年12月9日的巴蘭卡斯之役打通奧里諾科水道，1821年6月再取巴塞羅納。卡拉布索一役的部署最完整：玻利瓦爾把約四千至五千人分為三路縱隊，蘇克雷一線在中央高地以佯攻牽制王黨右翼，王黨在卡門山與科拉索納峽谷一線布防，雙方砲兵對射決定了高地歸屬；最後是帕埃斯率平原騎兵在拉斯克薩雷拉斯的中央以長矛密集衝鋒，擊穿王黨翼側，配合正面步兵與砲火推進。決定勝負的不是單一衝鋒，而是砲火、騎兵衝鋒與步兵推進在同一時段內的疊加。
tacticsEn: Three tactical systems ran through the war. The rising of 1811 was urban and militia-based: the Caracas militia formed up behind street barricades to meet the royalist columns with musket volleys and bayonet counter-charges; in June 1811 Miranda threw a force of a little over a thousand men against Puerto Cabello, whose garrison of fewer than five hundred held behind the walls and the gun positions, and the attackers were repulsed time and again, so that the First Republic lost its northern stepping stone. In 1812 the royalists changed to a dry-season offensive: Venezuela has a dry season and a rainy season, the royalist campaigning season ran from December to May, and their llanero horse gave them the mobility to work around the flooded marshes and creeks of the summer; on 26 March 1812 Caracas was struck by an extremely violent earthquake, the walls, barracks and magazines were largely destroyed, and the royalist army drove south at once, retaking Valencia in April, after which the insurgents fell back stage by stage towards the coast and Miranda finally left the country in July 1812, which allowed the royalists to restore their control of the northern littoral in 1814; what did it was not siegecraft but the window of the dry season. From 1813 to 1815 Bolívar rebuilt a force in the east, issued his decree of war to the death in April 1813, and his troops put a number of captured royalist officers to death after the recapture of the capital, the count varying from account to account; the royalist counterstroke was led by Boves' lancers, for a lance charge could break a packed infantry column in the narrow mountain tracks, and after La Puerta in June 1814 and El Topo in September 1814 the armies of the Third Republic were spent. The real reversal came with the war of endurance after 1816: Bolívar withdrew into the Orinoco basin, ran his government from a single-room hut with a carpenter's table and a printing press, promulgated the emancipation of the enslaved and the agrarian decrees, and kept the army supplied by river transport; in 1819 he took about two thousand men upstream from Angostura and over the Andes again, destroyed Barreiro at Boyacá on 7 August and entered Bogotá in December; in 1820 he turned to the northern front, the battle of Las Barrancas on 9 December reopening the Orinoco navigation, and Barcelona was taken in June 1821. The deployment at Carabobo is the most complete of the whole war: Bolívar divided roughly four to five thousand men into three columns, Sucre's line on the central heights feinting to pin the royalist right, the royalists holding a line across the Cerro del Carmen and the Cañada de la Corazona, and the duel between the two artillery parks deciding which side held the heights; the final stroke was Páez's llanero horse charging in a solid mass of lances at Las Queseras del Medio, tearing through the royalist flank in concert with the infantry and the guns pushing forward on the front. What decided the day was not any single charge but the superposition, within the same span of hours, of gunpowder fire, the cavalry charge and the infantry advance.
data: 有根據可寫的數字大致如下。1811年4月19日加拉加斯首倡獨立，7月5日第一共和國宣佈成立，1811年6月米蘭達攻打卡貝略港的兵力約一千出頭，守軍不足五百；1812年3月26日卡拉斯地震，烈度極強，城內城牆與軍械庫多毀。1813年4月6日發布至死方休令。1814年6月拉普艾塔、9月埃爾托波兩役，第三共和國覆亡。1816年玻利瓦爾翻越安第斯時所帶人數，諸說在一千至一千七百之間，同行者中凍餓病死者數百，軍隊在奧里諾科流域滯留一年有餘。1819年8月7日波亞卡之役，玻利瓦爾兵力約二千六百，王黨守軍約二千，交戰後俘獲約一千六百人，十餘門砲與大量軍械落入革命軍之手，12月10日進入波哥大；同年12月9日巴蘭卡斯之役打通奧里諾科航運。1821年6月24日卡拉布索之役，革命軍投入約四千至五千人，有說接近六千，王黨軍約一千八百至二千；革命軍傷亡約一千至一千二百，王黨死傷亦近一千，被俘者約一千八百至二千，繳獲野砲十九門、火槍約二千支。1821年6月28日拉斯克薩雷拉斯的中央一役，帕埃斯率數千平原騎兵擊破王黨翼側。大哥倫比亞成立時轄境逾百萬平方公里，涵蓋今委內瑞拉、哥倫比亞、厄瓜多與巴拿馬等地，人口以數百萬計，統計基準不同而數字互有出入；海地佩蒂安的援助包含一批火槍與一筆以萬計的款項。西班牙對委內瑞拉主權的正式承認要到1835年，兩國1845年簽訂和約。
dataEn: The figures that can be given on good authority are roughly these. On 19 April 1811 Caracas sounded its first cry of independence, and on 5 July the First Republic was proclaimed; in June 1811 Miranda attacked Puerto Cabello with a little over a thousand men against a garrison of fewer than five hundred. On 26 March 1812 Caracas was struck by an earthquake of extreme violence, which destroyed much of the walls and of the military stores. The decree of war to the death was issued on 6 April 1813. The Third Republic ended with the battles of La Puerta in June 1814 and El Topo in September. The size of the force Bolívar took over the Andes in 1816 is given in accounts ranging from a thousand to seventeen hundred men, several hundreds of them dying of cold, hunger and sickness on the way, and the army remained in the Orinoco basin for over a year. At the battle of Boyacá on 7 August 1819 Bolívar had about 2,600 men against some two thousand royalists, roughly sixteen hundred prisoners were taken and a dozen or more cannon and a great deal of matériel fell into the insurgents' hands, and Bogotá was entered on 10 December; the battle of Las Barrancas on 9 December of the same year reopened the Orinoco navigation. At Carabobo on 24 June 1821 the revolutionaries committed between four and five thousand men, by one account close to six thousand, against a royalist force of some eighteen hundred to two thousand; revolutionary casualties ran from about a thousand to twelve hundred, royalist dead and wounded came to close on a thousand as well, and something like eighteen hundred to two thousand men were taken prisoner, with nineteen field guns and about two thousand muskets captured. At Las Queseras del Medio on 28 June 1821 Páez's several thousand llanero horse broke the royalist flank. Gran Colombia at its founding covered more than a million square kilometres, embracing what are now Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador and Panama, with a population in the millions, the figures varying with the basis of the count. The aid from Pétion in Haiti included a batch of muskets and a sum of money in the tens of thousands. Spain's formal recognition of Venezuelan sovereignty did not come until 1835, and the two countries signed a treaty of peace and friendship in 1845.
cause: 要理解這場戰爭的起因，得把時間往回推到1808年。拿破崙的軍隊在巴約訥拘禁西班牙波旁王室，馬德里落入法軍之手，西班牙王位陷入危機，各殖民地議會在1810年被迫宣誓效忠斐迪南七世而自行治理，委內瑞拉的主要城市因此在1810年春天相繼成立自治政府；巴里納斯的金手杖起義即1810年8月何塞·菲利克斯·里巴斯率領的武裝暴動，開了風氣，1811年4月19日卡拉加斯公報刊出宣言，7月5日宣告獨立。深層原因是殖民體制本身的矛盾：十八世紀後期波旁改革把財政、壟斷與軍事集權收緊，1781年委內瑞拉的公社人起義與1790年代邊區的騷動都被鎮壓，知識階層與地方精英對都督區的治理方式與本土差別待遇早已不滿；米蘭達等一批參加過美國獨立戰爭與法國大革命的人，把共和與公民武裝的想法帶回故國。經濟上，拿破崙戰爭封鎖了西班牙與美洲的航運，蔗糖、可可與靛藍的出口受挫，軍費卻照加，財政壓力直接壓到殖民地上。1811年的共和國很快在軍事上失敗：米蘭達攻不下卡貝略港，1812年的地震與王黨的旱季反攻又摧毀了一切，1814年王黨恢復統治，鎮壓之後委內瑞拉的政治空間被封死，玻利瓦爾等一批軍人出走到海地與英屬安的列斯，玻利瓦爾在那裡得到佩蒂安的槍械與款項，並在1816年帶著數百人回到奧里諾科流域，決定以持久戰取代一場會戰，這才是1819年波亞卡與1821年卡拉布索得以成立的前提。1808年卡塔赫納宣言對總督的拒絕、1811年各省代表在卡塔赫納簽訂的聯盟條約，以及1816年東部各省的響應，說明美洲的分裂並非只有委內瑞拉一處。
causeEn: To understand the causes of this war one has to run the clock back to 1808. Napoleon's troops took the Bourbon king of Spain prisoner at Bayonne, Madrid fell to the French and the Spanish throne fell into crisis; in 1810 the colonial assemblies had perforce sworn allegiance to Ferdinand VII while governing themselves, and the principal cities of Venezuela accordingly set up autonomous governments in the spring of that year; the Golden Arm rising of Barinas, the armed revolt led by José Félix Ribas in August 1810, set the fashion, the Gaceta de Caracas published its manifesto on 19 April 1811, and independence was declared on 5 July. At a deeper level the war grew out of contradictions inside the colonial system: the Bourbon reforms of the later eighteenth century tightened finances, monopolies and military centralisation, the Comuneros rising of 1781 in Venezuela and the disturbances along the frontier in the 1790s were both put down, and the educated and the local elite had long resented the way the Audiencia governed and the discrimination between them and the mother country; men such as Miranda, who had served in the American War of Independence and in the French Revolution, brought back the ideas of a republic and of the citizen in arms. Economically, the Napoleonic war blockaded the shipping between Spain and America, exports of sugar, cacao and indigo suffered, the war charges went on rising, and the fiscal pressure fell straight onto the colony. The republic of 1811 failed militarily very quickly: Miranda could not take Puerto Cabello, and the earthquake of 1812 together with the royalist dry-season counter-offensive destroyed what was left; the royalists were restored in 1814, and after the repression the political space in Venezuela was shut, a number of soldiers such as Bolívar fled to Haiti and the British Antilles, and there Bolívar received the muskets and the money of Pétion before returning in 1816 with several hundred men to the Orinoco basin and deciding to substitute a war of endurance for a single decisive battle. That is the precondition for Boyacá in 1819 and Carabobo in 1821. The refusal of the viceroy in the Cartagena Manifesto of 1808, the federal pact signed at Cartagena in 1811 by the provincial representatives, and the response of the eastern provinces in 1816 all show that the fracture in the Americas was not confined to Venezuela.
impact: 這場戰爭的直接後果是西班牙在南美洲北部三百年的統治崩解：1821年6月24日卡拉布索之後，革命軍進入加拉加斯，委內瑞拉全境脫離王黨控制；1822年5月蘇克雷在皮欽查打敗皇家主義者，西班牙在南美洲最後的據點之一失守；1824年12月9日阿亞庫喬一役，蘇克雷擊潰何塞·德·坎特拉克率領的西班牙軍，秘魯全境光復，西班牙對美洲的戰爭在美洲本土軍隊手中收場，1826年最後的西班牙部隊撤出卡亞俄。制度上，1819年成立的大哥倫比亞聯邦把委內瑞拉、新格拉那達、基多與巴拿馬連為一體，是西語美洲規模最大的國家實驗；它維持了約十二年，1830年玻利瓦爾退出、委內瑞拉分離，其餘各省於1831年先後瓦解，聯邦解體過程留下的中央集權與聯邦之爭，開啟了委內瑞拉長久的內戰與考迪羅政治，也構成日後聯邦戰爭即1859至1863年戰爭的遠因。軍事上，解放者軍把正規步兵、砲兵與平原騎兵捏合成一支職業化軍隊，1820年代在加拉加斯設立的數學與繪畫軍事學校是西語美洲最早一批近代軍事技術教育機構之一，這支部隊後來在秘魯高原與安第斯山區的戰役中幾乎再無敗績，直到十九世紀末仍是南美陸軍的標杆。經濟上，殖民時代的壟斷被打破，開放貿易之後英國商人與1822年在倫敦籌得的貸款在委內瑞拉金融中佔了重要位置，1820年代可可樹病害席捲北部平原後，咖啡種植取而代之，委內瑞拉的出口結構從此改寫，帕拉瓜納半島的鹽田與平原畜牧則成為內陸的主要收入來源。國際上，這場戰爭把拉丁美洲帶進了世界地緣政治的主流敘述，玻利瓦爾的名號成為後世委內瑞拉與拉丁美洲一切政治訴求援引的符號。
impactEn: The direct consequence of the war was the collapse of three centuries of Spanish rule in northern South America: after Carabobo on 24 June 1821 the revolutionaries entered Caracas and the whole of Venezuela came out of royalist control; in May 1822 Sucre beat the royalists at Pichincha and one of the last Spanish strongholds in South America fell; at Ayacucho on 9 December 1824 Sucre destroyed the Spanish army led by José de Canterac and Peru was liberated, the war of Spain against America being brought to a close by armies of the Americas themselves, the last Spanish troops leaving Callao in 1826. Institutionally, the Gran Colombia federation founded in 1819 tied Venezuela, New Granada, Quito and Panama into one state, the largest state experiment in Spanish America; it held together for about twelve years, Bolívar withdrew in 1830 and Venezuela separated, the remaining provinces broke up one after another in 1831, and the quarrel between centralism and federalism left behind by the dissolution opened the long series of civil wars and caudillo politics in Venezuela and is the remote cause of the Federal War of 1859 to 1863. Militarily, the Libertador's army fused regular infantry, artillery and the llanero horse into a professional force, and the school of mathematics and drawing set up in Caracas in the 1820s was among the first modern schools of military technical education in Spanish America; that army was later almost unbeaten in the campaigns on the Peruvian plateau and in the Andes, and remained a model for the South American armies until the end of the nineteenth century. Economically, the colonial monopolies were broken, and after the opening of trade British merchants and the loan raised in London in 1822 came to hold an important place in Venezuelan finance; when the cacao disease swept the northern plains in the 1820s, coffee planting took its place and the export structure of the country was rewritten, while the salt pans of the Paraguaná peninsula and the stockbreeding of the plains became the main income of the interior. Internationally, the war carried Latin America into the mainstream narrative of world geopolitics, and the name of Bolívar became the sign every later political claim in Venezuela and Latin America would appeal to.
result: 分階段看結果。第一階段1811至1812年是失敗：米蘭達的共和軍攻不下卡貝略港，1812年3月的地震與王黨隨後的旱季反攻令北部重回王黨控制，共和國在同年7月名存實亡，米蘭達出走，1814年王黨恢復全區統治。第二階段1813至1815年仍以國軍收場：玻利瓦爾的至死方休令一度把王黨逼到東部山地，但1814年拉普艾塔與埃爾托波兩役之後第三共和國覆滅，玻利瓦爾再度流亡。第三階段1816至1821年才是真正的轉折：退入奧里諾科流域、以河運維持補給、以安第斯山脈的險道甩開追兵的持久戰法，換來1819年波亞卡的勝利與大哥倫比亞的成立，也換來1821年6月24日卡拉布索的決定性會戰，王黨右翼與砲兵陣地被奪，拉斯克薩雷拉斯的中央的騎兵衝鋒切斷退路，王黨軍崩潰，繳獲十九門野砲，成千被俘者被押往城裡，革命軍隨即進軍加拉加斯，委內瑞拉北部的控制權在一天之內易手。第四階段是跨國延伸：1822年皮欽查、1824年胡寧與阿亞庫喬，玻利瓦爾與蘇克雷的軍隊在秘魯高原擊潰西班牙主力，1826年最後一批西班牙軍隊撤出卡亞俄，戰爭以西班牙在南美洲的軍事存在終結收場。此後是政治層面的收尾：1826年卡尼亞達·德·戈麥斯停戰、1827至1828年瓜亞基爾會議、1830年大哥倫比亞解體與委內瑞拉獨立，1845年西委兩國和約簽訂，確認了1811年以來在戰場上取得的結果。
resultEn: Seen in stages, the result was this. The first stage, 1811 to 1812, was a failure: Miranda's republican army could not take Puerto Cabello, the earthquake of March 1812 and the royalist dry-season counter-offensive that followed returned the north to royalist hands, the republic was hollowed out by July of the same year, Miranda left, and in 1814 the royalists restored their rule over the whole province. The second stage, 1813 to 1815, likewise ended in defeat for the republic: Bolívar's decree of war to the death drove the royalists back into the eastern mountains for a time, but after La Puerta in June 1814 and El Topo in September the Third Republic collapsed and Bolívar was exiled once more. The third stage, 1816 to 1821, is where the real turning point lies: the withdrawal into the Orinoco basin, the supply of the army by river transport and the use of the Andean tracks to shake off pursuit, a war of endurance, brought the victory at Boyacá in 1819 and the founding of Gran Colombia, and brought the decisive battle of Carabobo on 24 June 1821, where the royalist right and its batteries were taken, the llanero charge at Las Queseras del Medio cut the way of retreat, the royalist army broke, nineteen field guns were captured, thousands of prisoners were marched into the town, and the revolutionaries entered Caracas, so that control of northern Venezuela changed hands within a single day. The fourth stage ran across frontiers: Pichincha in 1822, Junín and Ayacucho in 1824, where the armies of Bolívar and Sucre broke the main Spanish force on the Peruvian plateau, and the last Spanish troops leaving Callao in 1826, so that the war ended with the end of the Spanish military presence in South America. What followed was the political winding-up: the truce of Cañada de Gómez in 1826, the Congress of Guayaquil of 1827 to 1828, the dissolution of Gran Colombia and the independence of Venezuela in 1830, and the treaty of peace between the two countries in 1845 confirming what had been won on the field since 1811.
